description: We are Perceptron53 from AUST, Dhaka, Bangladesh
summary: PyroScope harmonizes 26 years of NASA MODIS (1 km, 2000–present) and VIIRS S-NPP (375 m, 2012–present) active-fire records into one continuous Burning Activity Calendar (FireCalendar) for early warning, wildland management, and emergency response. Across Bangladesh's 2012–2025 overlap, raw VIIRS detects 4.10x more hotspots than MODIS (39,193 vs. 9,645/year), creating an artificial 1.85x jump in 2012 when naively spliced. PyroScope resolves this by clustering 758,730 quality-filtered NASA FIRMS detections via Space-Time DBSCAN (2,700 m, 24 h) into 109,246 physical fire events, then applying cross-validated regional quantile mapping and ratio scaling to reduce the splice jump from 1.85x to 0.86x with zero unallocated events across 26,683 H3 cells. The web app reveals regional fire seasons—such as 97.07% of Chittagong Hill Tracts burning occurring in March–April—alongside anomaly calendars, advisory alerts, action checklists, nearby fire stations, and a tool-grounded Q&A assistant.
details:
What PyroScope Does & How It Works

PyroScope turns multi-sensor NASA FIRMS active-fire archives into a single, bias-corrected 2000–present Burning Activity Calendar across Bangladesh's 64 districts, 8 divisions, and the Chittagong Hill Tracts (CHT) preset, with support for custom bounding boxes.

Our pipeline processes 837,168 raw NASA FIRMS detections in four deterministic stages:

1. Quality Filtering: Applies sensor-appropriate filters—MODIS numeric confidence >= 30 and type = 0, and VIIRS categorical confidence ('n' or 'h') and type = 0 when present—retaining 758,730 reliable vegetation fire detections.

2. Space-Time Clustering: Runs Space-Time DBSCAN (2,700 m spatial radius, 24-hour window, min_pts = 2) per sensor family, grouping pixels into 109,246 discrete physical fire events and shrinking the annual VIIRS/MODIS gap from ~4.1x pixels down to ~1.5x events.

3. Regional Cross-Validated Harmonization: Over the 177 complete overlap months (2012-02 to 2026-10), districts with >= 3 mean monthly MODIS events calibrate directly (3 CHT districts), while 61 sparse districts fall back to parent division pools. Leave-one-year-out cross-validation selects between equal-n quantile mapping (1 unit) and ratio scaling (10 units), eliminating the naive 2012 splice jump (1.85x down to 0.86x).

4. Spatial Downscaling & Climatology: Proportions calibrated district totals down to 26,683 H3 resolution-7 cells with 0.0 unallocated events, then computes 2001–2025 monthly baselines (p50, p90, p95), elevated/extreme anomaly flags, and shortest circular 70% fire season windows.

Benefits & Intended Impact

- Eliminates False Sensor Spikes: Researchers and forest managers can distinguish true anomalous fire seasons (such as CHT's 2006 peak of 738 harmonized events or May 2020 extreme anomaly) from 2012 sensor-resolution artifacts.

- Local Early Warning & Action: Displays FireCalendar seasonal windows (CHT March–April holds 97.07% of harmonized annual activity), threshold alert subscriptions, role-based wildland mitigation checklists, English/Bangla language support, and nearby Bangladesh Fire Service & Civil Defence (102 / 999) stations.

- Grounded AI Q&A: "Ask PyroScope" answers questions in plain or standard language strictly via typed Parquet-backed tools—it never writes SQL or fabricates numbers—and includes a deterministic offline replay mode.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Stack

- Data Pipeline (Python 3.12): pandas, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn (BallTree), h3-py, GeoPandas, Shapely, PyArrow, DuckDB, uv.

- Backend API: FastAPI, Pydantic v2, DuckDB reading ZSTD Parquet tables, SQLite (alert subscription state), Google GenAI SDK (Gemini API + deterministic replay fallback).

- Frontend Web App: Next.js (App Router, TypeScript), Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, MapLibre GL via react-map-gl, deck.gl (H3HexagonLayer), Recharts, TanStack Query, pnpm.

- Testing & Deployment: pytest, ruff, mypy, Vitest, Docker Compose, GitHub Actions.

Creativity & Key Engineering Considerations

- Calibrate Regions, Then Downscale: Instead of unstable quantile mapping on sparse H3 cells, we calibrate at district/division scale and proportionally downscale so spatial sums remain 100% conserved.

- Scientific Transparency: Our /methodology page openly discloses calibration CV error, pre-Aqua Terra-only under-sampling (2000–2002), S-NPP single-sensor selection (avoiding 2018 NOAA-20 jump), and the advisory limitation that active-fire counts are not burned area.

Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure

SI tools (Antigravity, and Gemini API) were used to assist with software development and power the optional live mode of the in-app Ask PyroScope assistant. All scientific clustering, calibration, and statistical calculations are deterministic Python code verified by automated tests, and the assistant relies exclusively on typed API tools returning verified Parquet outputs (with an offline replay mode).
